lawyer:
Mr. TH Khan  & Mr. MA Wahhab Mia, Advocates  ----- For the Appellant.  
Mr. AKM Shamsul Karim, AAG  ----- For the State.
parties:
Ashrafuddin ----- Appellant 
 Vs. 
The State ----- Opposite Party.
full_judgment:
Muhammad Ansar Ali, J: This is a case of patricide. The appellant Ashrafuddin was put on trial to answer a charge under section 302 of the Penal Code and has been convicted under the said section of the Penal Code and sentenced to transportation for life by the Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh in Sessions Case No. 701 of 1982. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is, that on 2.9.82 AD corresponding to 16th Bhadra, 1389 BS at about 8.15 PM on Thursday the deceased Abdul Majid Mondal @ Pachu Moral asked his son Ashrafuddin to bring some kerosene oil from the shop of one Pair Hossain lying at a distance of about 300 yards but the accused refused to obey his father. At this the deceased rebuked the accused and asked him to get out of his sight. But the accused showed ill temper and did not leave the place. As a result the deceased became more angry and was about to beat the accused with a stick and the accused ran out of the house; that thereafter the deceased sat to his meals sitting on the prayer-chowki "নামাজের চৌকি" lying on the eastern side of the north-facing open verandah of the south bhiti tin roofed dwelling hut. The deceased was having meals in the light of one kupibati and his wife Asia Khatun, step-mother of the accused, was serving him meal and when she was coming with milk in a cup from the kitchen and reached half of the verandah where the deceased was taking his meal she saw the accused catching the deceased by neck with his left hand and laid him down from the chowki towards the south on the verandah and stabbed by a dagger in the left side of the chest of the deceased and Asia Khatun recognised the accused in the light of the said kupibati; that the deceased gave a jump towards the north and died there; on hearing the cries the informant's step-brother Aftabuddin and his full sister's husband Bachchu Mia PW 7 came to the spot from another nearby but towards north of the PO but and at the same time servants of the deceased namely, Shamsu PW 5, Jabbar, PW 6, Razzaque, PW 4 and Jalal came from the katchery ghar and other witnesses also came there and heard about the occurrence from Asia Khatun, PW 2; that the informant PW 1 also heard cries from his house at a distance of 100 to 150 yards from the PO house and came there and heard about the incident from Asia Khatun; that leaving the dead body to the relations the informant accompanied by dafadar Mutalib went to the Durgapur thana and lodged the First Information Report on 3.9.82 at about 3.15 PM and accordingly a case was started against the appellant under section 302 of the Penal Code. 

 3. PW 3 Shafiuddin Ahmed, Sub-Inspector of Police filled up the FIR form and thereafter PW 12 Md. Amir All took up the investigation of the case, visited the place of occurrence, seized alamat, held inquest over the dead body of the deceased Abdul Majid Mondal, prepared sketch map with index and then sent the dead body through Constable Muzammel Hoque, PW 13 to the morge at Netrokona hospital for post mortem examination of the deceased. The statement of witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was recorded and on completion of the investigation charge-sheet was submitted against the appellant under section 302 of the Penal Code. Thereafter the case was transmitted to the Court of the learned Sessions Judge, Mymensingh for trial. But the learned Sessions Judge transferred the case to the Court of the learned Additional Session Judge, Mymensingh for disposal. The learned Additional Sessions Judge was pleased to frame a charge against the appellant under section 302 of the Penal Code, to which the appellant pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. In all 14 witnesses were examined on behalf of the prosecution. 

 Mr. AKM Shamsul Karim, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing for the State, on the other hand, submits that the appellant has committed a heinous crime and has been rightly convicted and sentenced by the Additional Sessions Judge on proper consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record. He further submits that a court can convict an accused even on the evidence of a single witness under section 134 of the Evidence Act, if relied upon and that there may be some minor discrepancies here and there in the evidence of the witnesses in this case but the charge has been sufficiently established by reliable evidence on material points and as such the impugned order of conviction and sentence should be upheld. 

 10. In cross-examination this witness stated that his father married first at village Chamarganj and then married Jarina Khatun and thirdly Asarunnessa, fourthly Maleka Khatun at Village Gugla and fifthly Fatema at village Lengura and sixthly Asia Khatun. He further stated that his father divorced others keeping Jarina Khatun, his own mother Jarina and Asia. He stated that Asia previously was married to one Mohar Ali and she has a son Kasem by name by that husband. The witness stated that he has three (3) brothers (PW Hafiz and others) and one sister by his step-mother Jarina Khatun. He further states that he has 4 full brothers and 4 full sisters through mother Asarunnessa PW 8. It is stated that his father left son Moshiuddin and 3 daughters on the side of Asia Khatun. He also stated that PW Hafiz and PW Aftab are stepbrothers of the accused and PW 7 Bachchu Mia is their sister's husband and PW 6 Abdur Razzak, Abdul Jabbar and Shamsul are the yearly kamlas (servants) of the deceased's house. He admits that he cited the names of Anisur Rahman, Mukim Ali, Hussain Ali, Dafadar Mutalib and Jalal as witnesses in the FIR but they are not witnesses in the charge-sheet, though they are neighbours. He stated that Abdul Khaleque, PW 9 contested the election of local Chairman with the deceased on several occasions and Abdul Khaleque was the only political and social opponent of his father. He further admitted that Abdul Jabbar, Member, Mohim Ali, Abbas Ali, Azimuddin, Mannaf, Hussain Ali, Sahadat Fakir, Jalal, Lal Hussain Mia and Hussain were their close neighbours and the house of PW Khaleque was a little away from the house of the above witnesses. He states that PW Khaleque has suffered imprisonment as collaborator at the instance of his father. He admitted that he had no knowledge about actual occurrence but lodged the ejahar on the basis of what he had heard from PW 2 Asia Khatun. He stated that she (Asia) eloped with a servant named Polisha 6/7 months prior to the occurrence and she was recovered about a fortnight thereafter from the house of Bucha, a cousin of Polisha and the accused gave out the news of elopement with Polisha and their shelter at Bucha's house to his father. The accused was then promoted to class X from class IX and that his father whipped Asia Khatun after rescue and since then Asia was inimical to the accused. He states that his house is half mile away from his father's house and that PW Hafizuddin and PW Aftab reside at their Durgapur house. He stated that he came to the PO house in the night of occurrence at about 11.00 or 12.00 PM and found relations and neighbors there and Asia told none as to how the incident took place. He also found PW Abdul Khaleque there. He stated that the but of the deceased was on the south bhiti and the north facing parlour was on the east bhiti and there was a golaghar in the south of the parlour and east of the south bhiti hut. The place on the back of the south bhiti but was for urinal and the passage was in between the golaghar and the south bhiti hut. He stated that the dead body was lying at the mouth of the passage leading from the court-yard towards the urinal. This witness stated that Asia firstly told him that there was one like accused Ashraf who stabbed the deceased to death and then stated that it was the accused Ashraf who stabbed the victim. He further stated that Asia told him that Ashraf refused to carry out the order of his father to bring kerosene oil from a nearby shop of Pear Hossain and for that his father scolded him. He states that his father has 90/100 acres cultivable land. He called a darbar 10/12 days before his death to distribute his properties to the children of different wives and decided to give double shares to the accused including the house of Durgapur for his educational expenses and at this others opposed. In answer to a suggestion of the defence he stated that his father told him that Asia would get nothing in the property. He, of course, denied the suggestion that he conspired against the accused and falsely implicated him in this case. Defence suggestion was that the occurrence took place at a different time and in a different manner and that unknown assailant might have killed the deceased. He also denied the suggestion that the accused was implicated out of jealousy against him. 

 12. In her cross-examination she admitted that she was previously married to one Mohar Ali of village Horipur and she has one son named Kasem by that marriage. She stated that her father got divorce from that husband and after divorce she was given shelter by her Bhagnipati Amjad Ali and her sister gave her food and shelter. She stated that the nick-name of the deceased was Panchu Moral and there was no Kabin of her marriage with the deceased. She stated that her husband had two wives alive when she was married. She gave her age as 35. She denied her marriage with the servant Palashia. She once again admitted that Jabbar, Razzak and Shamsu were their labour who are still in their service and at the relevant time a boy servant and also another male servant were in the house. She stated the PW Hafiz stayed at Durgapur house but Aftab resided at village home. She also stated that the deceased asked the accused to bring kerosene oil instead of the servants as they were tired. She denied the suggestion that the story of kerosene oil and altercation was manufactured. She stated that the accused was heard to have uttered, “চুপ চুপ” 4/5 times to his father and she was in the kitchen to bring milk. She further stated that her husband was having meal and at the same time was calling the accused by name and that the exchange of abuse was for 4/5 minutes at least and not for 20/25 minutes. She stated that during exchange of abuse she was inside the kitchen and other inmates of the house did not come out to interfere. She did not also come to prohibit the accused. She further stated that the deceased was served with curry of fish and meat and he could eat well. She stated that she went to the kitchen without any lamp and volunteered to say that the night was moon-lit and she mentioned it to the 10. She states that the south bithi but is 22 cubits long, 12 cubits broad and the kitchen is to the west of this south bhiti but and the kitchen is 15/20 cubits from the place where the deceased was having meals. She stated that her husband fell on his back and cried out “আশ্রাফ মারিয়া ফেলল” She stated that she witnessed from a distance of 10/12 cubits that the accused was laying down the deceased by neck then she cried out. “আশ্রাফ একি করিতেছ, তোর বাবারে মারিয়া ফেলতেছ” she stated that giving out her first cry, She caught hold of her husband but nobody came on hearing the cry. She stated that the accused after giving the blow ran away by the southern gate of the house. She stated that she did not catch hold of her husband when he was attacked by the accused. She stated that when the deceased was caught by neck by the accused she could not jump upon him for protection. She stated that when the accused came with dagger, his father was taking meal and could not sec the dagger but she could see the dagger from a distance of 3/4 cubits but could not give him any caution. She stated that the deceased fell on the verandah from the chowki and did not fall on the passage near the court-yard and his entire body fell down on the verandah. She did not state to the daroga that her husband died in the court-yard. She stated that she caught hold of her husband and thereafter Bachchu and Ahab came who kept the body of the deceased on his back on the court-yard and that the place was between golaghar and the south bhiti but and there was an urinal behind the southern hut. She also stated that her husband died 3/4 minutes after the assault; there she her-self, Bachchu and Aftab also received blood-stain. She further stated that the victim died after 3/4 minutes of his lying on the court-yard. The wound of the victim was bounded by her shares but the daroga did not seize the same. The daroga also did not seize the blood-stained cloth of Bachchu and Aftab. She denied the suggestion that she did not state to the daroga about taking the dead body of the deceased on the court-yard. She admitted that she told the informant about falling of the deceased on the verandah and taking his dead body by Bachchu and Aftab on the court-yard. She denied the suggestion that her husband was killed by unknown assailant when he went out to make water. She also denied the suggestion that the occurrence did not take place at 8 or 8.30 PM or in the manner or at the place as alleged. She also denied the suggestion that a darbar took place 10/12 days be-fore the occurrence and in that Darbar it was settled that the accused would get double his share of the property including the house of Dargapur for his education and that she would not get anything. She denied the suggestion that she eloped with Polishia and took shelter at the house of Bachchu and on the information given by the accused she was recovered there-from and thereafter beaten by her husband. When examined by the prosecution she stated that a kupihati was burning on the stand at the time of occurrence. She stated that the house was a big one and that the kupihati was not shown when she was examined. She admitted that in their house there were 20/25 hurricanes. She denied the suggestion that the recognition of the accused at the time of taking meal of her husband in the light of the kupibati was false. 

 20. PW 9 Abdul Khaleque stated that once he was MP and that on 16th Bhadra, 1389 BS at about 8 or 8.30 PM Majid Mondal was murdered and he was then at his house, 300 to 400 yards away from the PO house. On hearing the cries, he came to the PO house and found the dead body of the deceased lying in the court-yard before the north verandah of the south bhiti but and the dead body was just below the verandah. He also found Majid, Aftab and wives of the deceased there and heard them to say that Ashraf murdered the deceased and the accused was not there. In cross-examination he stated that he was once chairman of the union but not so at the time of the murder and that deceased was also Union member. He denied the suggestion that the deceased contested with him in the chairmanship election. He admitted that he was in hajat for some days after liberation and denied the suggestion that the deceased was instrumental to that. He further denied the suggestion that he did not state to the I0 that all present at the place of occurrence told that Ashraf had killed his father. He also denied the suggestion that he did not find the accused at the place of occurrence and that the accused was also lamenting at the place of occurrence over the dead body of his father. On recall, he denied the suggestion that the occurrence did not take place at 8 or 8-30 PM and that the same did take place at mid-night. He stated that in the last chair-man election, the deceased had 'bullock cart' and Amjad 'Hukka' as symbols and that Amjad was elected. 

 22. PW 11 Aftabuddin, is the step-brother of the deceased. He stated that he was in the west bhiti but when his father was killed at 8 PM. Bachchu and he himself were sitting. He stated that he saw the accused Ashraf going to his father uttering and at that time he and Bachchu  (চুপ চুপ ) got out and heard cries of his step-mother Asia Khatun “আশ্রাফকে. Then they rushed to the spot and found the deceased lying on his chest on the verandah on chowki where he was taking meals. He stated that PW 2 Asia, PW 7 Bachchu took the dead body and laid it below the verandah in the court-yard contiguous to the verandah on its back. PW Asia told that accused Ashraf stabbed the deceased by dagger. In cross-examination he denied the suggestion that he did not state to Investigation Officer about 'Chup Chup' uttered by the accused and the cries of Asia (আশ্রাফ মারিয়া ফেলছে). He also denied the suggestion that he did not state to the Investigation Officer that he and Bachchu got out of the but on hearing Chup Chup or saw Ashraf approaching his father saying 'chup, chup. He stated that his father died immediately after he was placed on the court-yard. He admitted that his father was not dead while lying on the verandah and that deceased was not laid on the chowki over which he was having meals. He denied the suggestion that he did not tell the Investigation Officer about the fall of his father on verandah and removal of his body to the adjacent place of the courtyard by Asia, Bachcu and him-self. He denied the suggestion that he was giving tutored evidence to fill up the gap in the evidence. He also denied the suggestion that he was residing with his full brother Hafizuddin at Durgapur and that he came to the place of occurrence house after mid-might. He stated that the accused uttered 'Chup, Chup' threatening in a loud voice showing anger and temper while approaching the deceased. He volunteered to say that when stabbed by accused, his father cried saying “আশ্রাফ আমাকে মারিয়া ফেলছে). He stated that his father did not say anything in reply to 'Chup Chup'. He stated that they did not try to prevent the accused from doing so. He heard “আশ্রাফ আমাকে মারিয়া ফেলছে). He admitted that he did not see the act of stabbing the victim by the accused or his fleeing away on query by the court. He stated that when accused was approaching his father he saw the accused from inside the west-bhiti but as the track used by the accused was visible from the place where they had sat but his father was not visible. He stated that Ashraf made his entry through the north gate way while approaching the deceased. He stated that there was another gate to the south. He stated that the accused uttered 2/3 times, 'chup chup' and he saw the accused with a dagger in his hand while approaching his father in a mood of violence. He stated that there was no light in the north gate but volunteered to say that the night was moon-lit. He admitted that he could not raise any alarm when the accused was seen in such a mood He denied the suggestion that the accused was given double share of the property including the house at Durgapur. He admitted that his full brother Hafizuddin was residing at the Durgapur house. He denied the suggestion that they had conspired against the accused. He stated that at the time of occurrence he was staying at the place of occurrence house after appearing at the HSC examination. He denied the suggestion that the occurrence did not take place at the alleged time and in the alleged manner. 

 23. PW 12 Md. Amir Ali is the Investigating Officer in this case. He stated that he visited the place of occurrence, seized the alamats, held inquest over the dead body of the deceased, prepared sketch map with index, sent the dead body with Constable No.1715 Muzammel Huq to morgue, recorded statements of witnesses under section 161 of the Criminal Procedure Code and submitted charge-sheet. He proved the seizure list, sketch map, index, alamats namely, one kupibati, one blood stained pillow, one kupibati stand, blood stained earth and one blood stained garncha and one lungi. In his cross-examination he stated that in the inquest report there was mention as to who identified the dead body. He stated that Abul Hussain, Nikhil Chandra Debnath, Wafizuddi, Bisheswer Roy, Lashkoruddin and Hashimuddin were not charge-sheeted witnesses. He stated that none said to him that the dead body was shifted from the verandah to the court-yard and that there was no statement in the ejahar that the deceased fell on the verandah and that Asia, Bachchu and Altai) shifted him to the court-yard and kept the dead body on its back. He stated that the names of Anisur Rahman, Mukim Ali, Hussain Ali, Jalal and dafader Motaleb were shown as witnesses in ejahar. He stated that PW Asia Khatun did not say in her statement under section 161 of the Criminal Procedure Code that the deceased fell on the verandah wounded and she herself, Aftab and Bachchu shifted the body to the court-yard or that the night was moon-lit. PW Asia or Aftab or Bachchu did not show him any of their blood stained clothes. He stated that PW Asia told him that her husband (আশ্রাফ পড়িয়া গিয়া মারা যায়) and she did not state to him that her husband fell on the ground and she, Bachchu and Aftab (ধরাধরি করিয়া উঠানে রাখে). He stated that he got the dead body on the ground in the court-yard. He stated that PW 11 Aftabuddin did not tell him that he had seen the accused proceeding towards his father uttering 'Chup, Chup' with dagger in the moon-lit night or that he heard loud cry of his step-mother saying (আশ্রাফ মারিয়া ফেলছে). He stated that PW 11 Aftabuddin did not state that his father was lying on his chest in the verandah or that Asia, Bachchu and he himself carried the wounded victim to the court-yard from the verandah or that he saw accused Ashraf enter through the north gate. He gave the description of the sketch map as follows:—B is south bhiti but and C is kitchen, C. is 4/5 cubits away from western end of 'B'. There is no mention of gates and location thereof. He stated that C is the Golaghar and A is the Court-yard. 

 30. PW 1 stated in his deposition that the occurrence took place at the house of the deceased on 2.9.82 at about 8.30 PM, but he was not a eye-witness of the actual occurrence. He only heard from PW 2 Asia Khatun about the occurrence. But he has stated one thing about the story of bringing kerosene oil that when accused was asked to bring kerosene oil by his father he refused and thereupon his father the victim rebuked him in the late afternoon before sunset. He also stated that at about 8 PM his lather was served with meals by PW 2 Asia Khatun who had gone to bring milk from the kitchen and on her return she found the deceased attacked and killed by the accused. From this it appears that the story of bringing kerosene oil and altercation of the deceased was before sunset and when PW 2 Asia Khatun went to bring milk, it appears that the deceased had already finished his meal. In cross-examination this witness stated about the story of elopement of Asia Khatun PW 2 with their servant Polishia. He also stated about the enmity that developed between PW Asia and the accused Ashrafuddin, as accused Ashraf gave out the information about the elopement and the place where-from she was found out and subsequently beaten by her husband the deceased. He stated that he came to the place of occurrence house at about 11 or 12 PM and found the relations and neighbours including PW Khaleque at the place of occurrence. He stated that there was a place behind the south bhiti-hut used as urinal and also passage between the golaghar and the south bhiti but and that the dead body was lying in the north leading to the urinal. He also admitted the fact that in a darbar held 10/12 days before the death of the deceased, it was decided to give the accused double his share including the house at Durgapur for his education and the other heirs of the deceased seriously opposed the same. Thus the evidence of PW 1 does not support the prosecution case, rather it supports the de-fence plea. Now Asia Khatun PW 2 is the main witness in this case. She states that the alleged occurrence took place at about 8 or 8-30 PM when she was serving the victim her husband with food who sat upon a namazi chowki in the eastern side of their north facing hut. She raised the question of shortage of kerosene oil before the victim who asked his son accused Ashraf to fetch the same from a nearby shop but Ashraf refused when he was threatened by his father, the victim and then some altercation took place between them. But according to P W 1, this part of the prosecution case about fetching kerosene oil took place in the afternoon before sun-set. It appears from the evidence of PW 2 that she raised the question of fetching shortage of kerosene at the time of serving her husband with food at about 8-30 PM. It further appears that after serving meal she went to the kitchen to bring milk for her husband and at that time the accused came with a dagger and laid his father the victim by neck upon the chowki, uttered the word “চুপ চুপ” and then gave 2 dagger blows, one in the left side of the chest and the other one in the left hand of the victim who thereupon fell on his chest on the ground of the verandah of the south-bhiti hut, and on the cry of PW 2 Asia, PW 7 Bachchu, PW 11 Aftab came there and they together placed the victim on his back on the court-yard at a place between the golaghar and the south bhiti but behind which there was an urinal and the victim died 3/4 minutes thereafter. She further states that there was a kupi burning at that time and she saw from a distance of 10/12 cubits the laying down of the victim by the accused but could not do anything for this protection. She also states that her husband fell on his back and cried out “আশরাফ মরিয়া ফেলল”. Now, if the evidence of PW 2 is considered along with the evidence of other witnesses, it will be found that apart from the fact that she is an interested witness who had grudge against the accused, her deposition on material points particularly with regard to the time, place and the manner of occurrence is extremely contradictory and suffers from inherent improbabilities. So far the time of occurrence, she stated that it was about 8/8-30 PM but from the evidence of other PWs. namely PW 4, PW 5, PW 7 it appears that the time of the alleged occurrence was different. According to PWs. 4 and 5, the alleged occurrence took place at dead night and according to PW 7 Bachchu it took place at about 11 or 12 PM. PW 9 and PW 1, of course have stated that the occurrence took place at about 8 or 8-30 PM but PW 9 Abdul Khaleq is not an eye-witness of the occurrence, His evidence is a hearsay evidence and does not inspire confidence. PW Aftabuddin, however stated that the victim was killed at 8 PM and and at that time he along with PW 7 Bachchu were in the west-bhiti but of the deceased's house. But this PW 7 Bachchu did not say so rather he denied the suggestion of the prosecution that the occurrence took place at 8 or 8.30 PM. He also denied the suggestion of the prosecution that the heard the cries of the deceased to the effect that “আশ্রাফ মাইরা ফেলছে আমারে”. He also denied to have heard about any quarrel between the deceased and the accused over bringing kerosene oil from a shop. It appears from the suggestion of the defence as well as from the evidence of PW 1 that there was dispute and dissension amongst the heirs of the deceased including PW 1, PW 2 and PW 11 over their shares in the properties of the victim and a salish was held there over such dispute and naturally PW 11 Aftab, a step-brother of the deceased, had jealousy and grudge against the accused appellant who was allegedly given double his share by the deceased. So, this witness also appears to be highly interested witness. He stated that at the time of occurrence he along with PW 7 Bachchu were sitting inside the west bhiti but of the deceased hut. PW 7 denied the same. PW 11 Aftabuddin stated that he saw the accused going towards his father uttering “চুপ চুপ” and at that time he himself and P W 7 Bachchu got out and heard cries of PW 2 Asia Khatun “আশ্রাফ মারিয়া ফেলছে” But PW 7 Bachchu did not say so. Further PW 12 the Investigation Officer stated that PW 11 Aftabuddin did not tell him that he had seen the accused proceeding towards his father with dagger uttering 'chup chup' or that he heard loud cry of his step-mother Asia Khatun PW 2 saying “আশ্রাফ মারিয়া ফেলছে”. It has been further stated by PW 12 that PW 11 Aftab did not state to him that his father was lying on his chest in the verandah or that Asia PW 2, Bachchu PW 7 and he himself carried the victim to the courtyard from the verandah or that he had seen accused Ashraf entering through the north gate of the house. Thus it is very difficult for us to place reliance upon PW 11 Aftabuddin. Further, it appears as something unusual and improbable that he would be seeing such a violent mood of the accused with a dagger in hand moving towards his father fir attacking him (father), but he would be doing nothing and even would not be raising any alarm to prevent the accused, his step-brother, from resorting to such a heinous action. He, of course, admitted that he did not see the act of stabbing the victim by the accused or his fleeing away from the place of occurrence. 

 31. Further the evidence of PW 14 the doctor to the effect that the victim was about 75 years and at least 4/5 hours time was necessary for complete digestion of food for him and that his stomach was found empty goes to belie the time of occurrence as given by the prosecution and supports that of the defence. Therefore we find that the prosecution has failed to prove the time of occurrence as alleged. Now, let us see how far the prosecution has been able to prove the place of occurrence as given in its case. According to the solitary eye-witness, PW 2 Asia the place of occurrence is the eastern verandah of the north facing south bhiti but of the deceased, and when the victim fell on the verandah, he was shifted therefrom to the courtyard nearby and placed on his back. But PW 1 said that he found his father lying dead on the pathway in between the east and the south bhiti huts. PW 4 said that he found the deceased lying on the corner of the south bhiti hut. PW 5 said that he found the dead body lying in between the south bhiti but and the golaghar in front of the verandah. PW 7 denied a suggestion by the prosecution that he himself and PW 11 Aftab found the deceased lying on the verandah on his chest and they jointly took the victim in the passage and placed him on his back. PW 9 said that he found the dead body of the victim lying in the courtyard before the north verandah of the south bhiti hut. PW 11 said that he found the deceased lying on his chest on the verandah on a chowki where he was taking meal. But PW 1 in his cross-examination stated that the dead body was lying at the mouth of the passage from the courtyard towards the urinal. Thus from the above evidence, it appears that the prosecution could not establish by reliable evidence the actual place of occurrence and falling down of the victim after the alleged stabbing. Had the occurrence taken place on the verandah of the north facing south bhiti but of the deceased, then why the victim while still alive after the alleged stabbing, would be taken to the courtyard or on the passage from the courtyard to-wards the urinal, instead of keeping him on the verandah and taking necessary step for his treatment? Thus it appears that the PWs. are not uniform in de-scribing the place of occurrence and the prosecution has failed to satisfactorily establish the same as alleged. Now, let us see whether the occurrence has taken place in the manner as alleged. PW 1 the informant stated that there was altercation between the victim and his son the accused over fetching kerosine oil in the late afternoon before sunset. PW 2 Asia Khatune also stated about the said altercation but further stated that it had taken place at the time when the victim was being served with meal by herself at 8 PM. There is no any other witness to corroborate her on this point. Admittedly the deceased had a number at servants in his house but instead of asking any one of them to fetch kerosine oil, it is not understood why the victim would ask his son the accused to fetch kerosine oil from a shop at night particularly when the son was a student. Again PW 7 stated that he had not heard about any quarrel between the deceased and the accused over bringing kerosine oil from a neighbouring shop. To us it appears that this part of the prosecution story is nothing but a concoction to the prosecution case. Then about serving meal to the victim by PW 2 in the eastern verandah of the south bhiti but at 8 PM on 2.9.82, there is no evidence on record to corroborate PW 2. PW 8 Asarunnessa, another wife of the deceased, though tendered by the prosecution but cross-examined by the defence stated that her husband used to have meals in a room inside the south bhiti hut. Thus the story of having meal by the victim at the place and time as given by PW 2 is not above doubt or suspicion. The further prosecution story of arrival of the accused with dagger in hand uttering the word 'Chup Chup' and laying down the victim by neck on the chowki and then stabbing him with the dagger as narrated by PW 2 is also without any corroboration by any of the witnesses. PW 11 Aftabuddin, of course, said that he along with PW 7 Bachu were sitting inside the west bhiti but and they had seen therefrom the accused in a violent mood to enter into the PO house through the north gate and to rush towards the victim but he had not done any-thing to prevent the accused from committing the alleged offence. This is something unusual. Further-more PW 7 Bachu did not say so, Besides, PW 1 I admitted that his father the victim was not visible from the room wherein he was sitting along with PW 7 Bachu and he had not seen the actual occurrence of stabbing the victim. Thus the evidence of PW 2 remains without any actual corroboration. As we have already observed that enmity developed between this PW Asia and the said accused and also between the said accused and PW 11 Aftab for the reasons as suggested by the defence and evidenced by PW 1, These two witnesses are not at all disinterested. Moreover, their evidence appear to have material discrepancies and the same suffers from inherent improbabilities. The death of the victim is not disputed but the question is whether there is sufficient reliable evidence to connect the accused appellant with the above killing of the de-ceased. It has been submitted by the learned Advocate for the State that evidence of PW 2, the alleged eye-witness, is enough to prove the prosecution case and to find the accused guilty of the charge. It is of course true that in view of section 134 of the Evidence Act, the conviction of an accused can be based even upon the evidence of a single witness, if believed but that witness must be wholly reliable. Generally speaking oral testimony in this context may be classified into three categories, namely, (1) wholly reliable, (2) wholly unreliable and (3) neither wholly reliable nor wholly unreliable. In the first category of proof, the court should have no difficulty in coming to its conclusion either way, it may convict on the testimony of a single witness if it is found to be above reproach or suspicion of interestedness, incompetence of subordination. In the second category, the court equally has no difficulty in coming to its conclusion. it is in the third category of cases that the court has to be circumspect and has to look for corroboration in material particulars by reliable testimony direct or circumstantial. This view has been expressed in the case of Vadivelu Thevar. Vs. The State of Madras reported in 1957 PLD (SC) Ind 525 and we are in full agreement with the same. In the light of the above decision, if this case is examined, it will be found that PW 2 Asia Khatun is the only alleged eye-witness for the prosecution and from the above discussion of her evidence it can be safely said that she is not at all wholly reliable, if not wholly unreliable and as such effective and sufficient corroboration of her evidence in material particulars in essentially necessary by reliable testimony to base conviction of the accused under section 302 of the Penal Code. But in the instant case as discussed above, there is no such evidence of corroboration. Hence we are in extreme difficulty to rely on the evidence of PW 2, the only alleged eye-witness to uphold the conviction of the accused appellant. It also strikes us from the point of probability and improbability that when the accused was being favoured with more than his share in the property by his father why he would be so turbulent and ferocious to kill him upon a petty matter of fetching kerosine oil. So, the possibility of false involvement of the appellant in the case cannot be brushed aside. 

 In the result, the appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh is set aside and the appellant is acquitted of the charge brought against him. Let the appellant be set at liberty forthwith if not wanted in connection with any other case. Send down the lower court's records expeditiously.
